topics.label: Introduction and lecture objectives
topics.groupedBecause: Opening framing outlining the lecturer's background, course structure, and learning objectives regarding cancer causation.

topics.label: Intrinsic, genetic, and evolutionary bases of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the core concept of cancer as a microevolutionary genetic disease driven by endogenous mutation sources and inherited predispositions.

topics.label: Environmental risk factors, epidemiology, and cancer causation debates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics survey known environmental carcinogens, discuss public and scientific debates on 'bad luck' versus exposure, and evaluate epidemiological variation in global cancer rates.

topics.label: Infectious agents and viral oncogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how infectious pathogens drive cancer development, highlighting Burkitt lymphoma as a multi-factorial model of viral carcinogenesis.

topics.label: Chemical and physical mutagens and metabolic activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the biochemical mechanisms by which radiation and metabolized chemical carcinogens induce direct DNA damage and bulky adducts.

topics.label: Tumor initiation versus promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define the distinction between mutagenic initiators and non-mutagenic promoters that stimulate clonal proliferation and chronic inflammation.

topics.label: Developmental susceptibility and summary of carcinogenic mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how developmental timing affects organ susceptibility to carcinogens and summarise the primary mechanistic modes of cancer induction.

topics.label: Methodologies for identifying and testing carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the sequencing, epidemiological, animal in vivo, and in vitro experimental approaches used to detect and evaluate carcinogenicity.

topics.label: Concluding perspective on balancing carcinogenic risk and benefit
topics.groupedBecause: Closing framing reflecting on everyday risk-benefit decisions regarding carcinogen exposure and summarising the key takeaways of the lecture.
